title: Dispatch: legacy stable-recovery adoption migration (attempt 1)
description:
Works defect bead eshyra-q93i (read it first: full analysis with file/line refs). Parent spec: eshyra-geny (acceptance criterion 2). NOTE: branched after the eshyra-r2ps/cc3c dispatch merged — `advanceWorldTime` now resolves recoveries inside its clock transaction; keep that invariant.

Branch/worktree: this bead's id, cut from eshyra-geny.

## Code survey (verified 2026-07-19)

- `packages/core/data/migrations/0020_stable_recovery_deadline.sql`: adds the three nullable schedule columns, no backfill. Migrations are checksummed/immutable — never edit an existing migration; add a new one (next free number after the current highest; 0021 was the highest on main when this was written — re-check in your worktree).
- `packages/core/src/state/hpLifecycle.ts:597-626` `resolveStableRecoveries`: WHERE clause silently skips stable-at-zero rows with any NULL schedule field.
- `packages/core/src/state/hpLifecycle.ts:138` `scheduleStableRecovery`: roll = 1d4, anchor = clock.elapsed_minutes, deadline = anchor + roll*60. Column CHECKs: roll BETWEEN 1 AND 4, anchor/deadline >= 0.
- `stabilizeCharacter` (line 555) rejects non-dying characters, so legacy rows have no repair path today.
- Migration runner: `packages/core/src/persistence/migrationRunner.ts`; existing migration tests give the pattern for testing a new migration against a pre-seeded legacy DB.

## Supervisor decision (implement this option)

Deterministic SQL backfill in a NEW migration, plus fail-closed resolver:

1. New migration `00NN_stable_recovery_adoption.sql` (next free number): for every character row with `life_state='stable' AND hp_current=0` and any of the three schedule columns NULL, set ALL THREE: `stable_recovery_roll = 4`, `stable_recovery_anchor_elapsed_minutes = (SELECT elapsed_minutes FROM clock WHERE id=1)`, `stable_recovery_deadline_elapsed_minutes = anchor + 240`. Rationale (document in the migration header comment): the original 1d4 roll is unrecoverable; 4 hours is the SRD maximum, deterministically chosen so migrated characters are never woken EARLIER than any outcome the real roll could have produced; anchor is adoption time because the original stabilization time was never persisted. Guard the clock subquery: if the clock row is missing/NULL, the migration must fail loudly rather than write NULL/garbage (COALESCE-to-0 silently is NOT acceptable; prefer a technique that makes the UPDATE violate a CHECK or an explicit failing statement).
2. `resolveStableRecoveries`: after the existing due-row query, add a detection query for rows with `life_state='stable' AND hp_current=0` and at least one NULL among the three schedule columns — throw MutateStateError naming the character id(s) (fail closed; post-adoption these indicate corruption). Partially populated (some NULL, some not) must also throw, and this check must run regardless of whether any row is currently due.

## Tests

- Migration test (follow existing migration-test patterns): seed a DB at the pre-adoption schema state with a stable-at-zero character with NULL schedule fields + a clock at a known elapsed_minutes; run migrations; assert roll=4, anchor=clock value, deadline=anchor+240; then assert clock advance past the deadline recovers the character through the normal path. Also: a stable-at-zero character that ALREADY has all three fields keeps its original values; dying/conscious characters untouched.
- Resolver fail-closed test: hand-corrupt one schedule field to NULL on a stable-at-zero character → resolveStableRecoveries throws (and names the character).

## Verification

`npm run verify:worktree` from this worktree (run `npm ci` first). Do not weaken existing tests. Commit on this branch only.
notes: Implemented migration 0022 stable-recovery adoption and resolver fail-closed validation. Legacy stable-at-zero rows with incomplete schedules are deterministically assigned roll 4, adoption-time anchor, and +240-minute deadline; missing/invalid clock state fails through NOT NULL/CHECK constraints. Added migration adoption/preservation/normal-recovery/missing-clock tests and partial-schedule corruption coverage. npm ci passed; npm run verify:worktree passed (261 files, 4656 tests passed, 4 skipped files, 19 skipped tests). No follow-up beads discovered.
